key_insight: ConGLUDe is a single contrastive geometric model that unifies structure- and ligand-based drug-design training by learning a shared embedding space where proteins and ligands that interact are pulled together, enabling joint use of both data sources at scale.
problem_solved: Traditional pipelines treat structure-based (protein–ligand complexes) and ligand-based (SMILES/assay) design separately, limiting transfer of information and scale; ConGLUDe removes this gap by training one model to leverage both modalities simultaneously.
method: Geometric protein encoder produces whole-protein representations and implicit embeddings of predicted binding regions using 3D-aware (equivariant) features.
Contrastive learning couples the protein encoder with ligand encoders so that true protein–ligand pairs map close in a shared latent space while negatives are pushed apart.
Unified training uses both structure-based examples (complexes) and ligand-only data, enabling cross-modal transfer for tasks like pocket prediction, virtual screening, and ligand generation.
impact: Provides a single, scalable foundation model for multiple drug-design tasks, improving data efficiency and making it easier for ML practitioners to build end-to-end design pipelines that exploit both structural and ligand information.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: two encoders (protein geometric + ligand) with a central contrastive loss and shared embedding space.
Embedding scatterplot: proteins and their true ligands clustered together vs. random negatives to show contrastive alignment.
Workflow infographic: unified training data sources (structures + ligands) → single model → downstream tasks (screening, scoring, generation).
Performance bar chart: relative gains or benefits (e.g., transferability, data-efficiency) versus separate SBDD/LBDD baselines.
paper_title: Contrastive Geometric Learning Unlocks Unified Structure- and Ligand-Based Drug Design
paper_authors: Lisa Schneckenreiter, Sohvi Luukkonen, Lukas Friedrich, Daniel Kuhn, Günter Klambauer
